 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Los Angeles Rams have been a tough team to figure out this season. They've only won six games and are lacking a statement win, but looking at their roster, it's hard to find many players who are performing well below expectations.
 After their Week 11 bye, the Rams will need to be almost perfect in their final seven games . And if they're going to reach the playoffs, they'll need these four players to rise to the occasion and play better than they have.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement QB Matthew Stafford
 Few people expected Stafford to have another MVP-type season this year after winning the award in 2025, but he hasn't looked like the same quarterback. He's not seeing the field as well, throwing inexplicable interceptions where he either didn't read the defense right or overlooked an underneath defender. His accuracy is also a little bit off, missing throws downfield that he would ordinarily make – and consistently did last year.
 If the Rams are going to make a run to the playoffs and beyond, they need Stafford to play the way he did last year. This league-average play won't cut it, especially with all the injuries Los Angeles is dealing with on offense.
 WR Tutu Atwell
 Puka Nacua will have to miss at least three more games. Davante Adams has a chance to return against the Packers, but it's not certain. Therefore, it could be another week of Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith and CJ Daniels leading the wide receivers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mumpfield flashed his potential as the No. 1 receiver against the Cardinals, but Atwell needs to be better. His 31-yard catch on fourth-and-6 was a big play in the game, and though he shouldn't be expected to make such catches game in and game out, he should be someone Stafford can rely on. He has the experience and speed to be a difference-maker.
 RG Kevin Dotson
 The Rams' O-line has been decimated by injuries in the last two weeks, losing Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon to multi-week injuries. Dotson has long been a standout at right guard, but he needs to be even better now that the Rams are down to their third-string center and left guard.
 Dotson has already allowed 19 pressures this season, which is just three fewer than he gave up all of last year. He has room to be better down the stretch, and the Rams will need him to be with all the injuries they've suffered on the offensive line.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement S Kam Curl
 Curl is an incredibly valuable player in the secondary, more than proving his worth last season – particularly in the playoffs. This season, though, he hasn't been quite as impactful. He's missed a team-high nine tackles and has allowed receptions on 15 of his 18 targets, giving up two touchdowns with one pass breakup.
 Kam Kinchens and Quentin Lake can both improve, too, but if Curl can be a playmaker on the back end for Los Angeles, it'll go a long way.
